No bug that would make the result meaningless. The repair step still runs, and with less search time the run stays well under the 45 s limit.

Recomputed z: improvement = incumbent - candidate = -2.9317 - (-2.9301) = -0.0016 (the candidate is worse). Standard error = 0.0034 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/2) ≈ 0.00416, so z ≈ -0.38. The harness reports -0.362. The gap fits rounding of the 4-decimal values (a true gap of about 0.0015 gives -0.362), so the sign and size agree.

The comparison rests on 1 candidate run against 2 incumbent runs, so the evidence is weak either way. Still, cutting the search time to 30% would be expected to make results worse, and the data agrees, so the provisional reject is consistent.
